problem: Instruction-following agents must pick actions from both the instruction and the current situation, and must react immediately as speech arrives. Utterance-level, non-incremental systems cannot do this.
motivation: Human navigational instructions are given in dynamically changing situations, so the agent has to act on partial spoken input using obstacle locations and its own movement history. A demonstrable system is also useful for collecting human-robot interaction data in such situations.
key_idea: A simulated mobile robot in a 3D virtual environment incrementally understands spoken navigational instructions and controls itself immediately, combining the incremental understanding results with situation information (obstacle locations, moving history).
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablations or analysis can be cited. The paper suggests that combining incremental language understanding with situational context enables immediate reactions and doubles as a data-collection platform for interactions in dynamic settings.
method: Incremental understanding: interprets spoken instructions word by word or chunk by chunk as they arrive, rather than waiting for the end of the utterance.
Situated action selection: chooses robot actions from the incremental understanding results together with situation information (obstacle locations, moving history).
Immediate control: drives a mobile robot in a 3D virtual environment as the instruction unfolds.
Data collection use: the system serves as an experimental platform for collecting human-robot interactions in dynamically changing situations.
